original.prompt: In March 2026, India changed its rules on foreign direct investment from land-bordering countries. Consider the following statements about the change:
items: Investments where Chinese beneficial ownership stays below 10% now enter through the automatic route.
Proposals in electronics, batteries, rare-earth magnets, capital goods and solar cells will receive a government decision within 60 days, provided Indian residents retain majority control.
The relaxation applies only to investments from China and not to other land-bordering neighbours.
original.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
original.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the change is part of a broader policy covering all land-bordering neighbours, though it is squarely aimed at rebuilding commercial ties with Beijing. Under the previous policy, any firm with a Chinese beneficial owner needed government approval regardless of stake, which caught global PE and VC funds with Chinese limited partners.
original.source: Now, investments where Chinese beneficial ownership stays below 10% enter through the automatic route.
